audits.title: Using a national guideline: an audit of the management of gonorrhoea in Newcastle upon Tyne.
audits.standard: National gonorrhoea guideline with auditable targets
audits.setting: Genitourinary Medicine Department, Newcastle General Hospital

cycle1.result: Chlamydia screening or presumptive treatment 98%; effective first-line therapy 95.4%; test of cure within one month 68.2%; partner notification discussion documented 94.3%; partner attendance 65%.

audits.other_findings: Microscopy sensitivity 90.4% for male urethral and 26.6% for female genital gonorrhoea; culture sensitivity 98.5%.
audits.citation: Watson PG. Using a national guideline: an audit of the management of gonorrhoea in Newcastle upon Tyne. Int J STD AIDS. 2000;11(10):677-681. doi:10.1258/0956462001915057. PMID: 11057940.

audits.title: Audit of gonorrhoea test of cure at the genitourinary medicine department in Newcastle upon Tyne, UK.
audits.standard: National guidelines stating that test of cure is usually performed
audits.setting: Genitourinary medicine department, Newcastle General Hospital

cycle1.result: Of 126 cases with test of cure after a sensitive antibiotic, none were positive.

audits.other_findings: Year 2000 cases were also analysed: none of 125 tests of cure were positive, questioning the need for routine test of cure.
audits.citation: Holland TM, Hussey J, Pattman RS, Sankar KN, Faldon CM. Audit of gonorrhoea test of cure at the genitourinary medicine department in Newcastle upon Tyne, UK. Int J STD AIDS. 2003;14(9):630-631. doi:10.1258/095646203322301103. PMID: 14511501.

audits.title: A national audit of gonorrhoea management.
audits.standard: Auditable outcome measures in the National Guideline for the Management of Gonorrhoea in Adults and evidence-based outcome standards (Low et al.)
audits.setting: 93 genitourinary medicine clinics in the UK (BASHH National Audit Group postal survey)

cycle1.result: Auditable outcome measures and outcome standards were broadly being met.

audits.citation: Price IH, Menon-Johansson A, Daniels D, National Audit Group of the Association for Sexual Health and HIV. A national audit of gonorrhoea management. Int J STD AIDS. 2006;17(2):133-134. doi:10.1258/095646206775455676. PMID: 16464279.

audits.title: An audit on the management of gonorrhoea at the Whittall Street Clinic, Birmingham, UK.
audits.standard: National recommendations for gonorrhoea management (nine auditable standards)

cycle1.result: 4 men and 9 women not given appropriate antibiotic; 7 women untreated; 0.33 partners contacted per case; HIV testing uptake 64%; oropharyngeal swabs in 34% with oral sex history; only 3 of 9 standards met.

audits.intervention: Staff retraining, updated local protocols, routine offer of test of cure and methods to improve partner notification were implemented.
audits.other_findings: Treatment failure in 3 of 33 patients with test of cure.
audits.citation: Sawyer R, Manavi K. An audit on the management of gonorrhoea at the Whittall Street Clinic, Birmingham, UK. Int J STD AIDS. 2007;18(5):354-356. doi:10.1258/095646207780749745. PMID: 17524202.

audits.title: An audit of pharyngeal gonorrhoea treatment in a public sexual health clinic in Adelaide, South Australia.
audits.standard: Local protocol of ceftriaxone 250 mg with test of cure; CDC 2010 and BASHH 2011 gonorrhoea guidelines

cycle1.result: Six test-of-cure failures over 11 years among 215 patients treated for pharyngeal gonorrhoea.

audits.other_findings: Local isolates less sensitive to ceftriaxone rose to 11.6% in 2010 from 5.3% in 2009.
audits.citation: Hustig A, Bell C, Waddell R. An audit of pharyngeal gonorrhoea treatment in a public sexual health clinic in Adelaide, South Australia. Int J STD AIDS. 2013;24(5):399-400. doi:10.1177/0956462412472792. PMID: 23970709.

audits.title: A re-audit of the management of gonorrhoea.
audits.standard: Auditable outcomes for gonorrhoea management (national guideline outcomes)

cycle1.result: Three of eight auditable outcomes met.

audits.intervention: New measures introduced after the first audit; electronic patient records with patient record templates introduced December 2012

cycle2.result: Six of nine auditable outcomes met.

audits.other_findings: Improved documentation through record templates was thought to contribute considerably.
audits.citation: Ekanayaka R, Challenor R. A re-audit of the management of gonorrhoea. Int J STD AIDS. 2016;27(9):801-804. doi:10.1177/0956462415625176. PMID: 26738518.

audits.title: Staff, associate specialist and specialty doctors' national audit on the management of gonorrhoea in the United Kingdom, 2015.
audits.standard: BASHH 2011 gonorrhoea guideline auditable outcomes (first-line treatment, chlamydia screening/treatment, test of cure, written information, partner notification) and 2012 testing guideline
audits.setting: UK sexual health services (national SAS doctors' audit)

cycle1.result: 83% received first-line treatment (reason given for not doing so in 11%); test of cure documented for 62%; written information offered to 41%.

audits.other_findings: Supplementary NAAT testing results inconsistent; other outcomes satisfactory.
audits.citation: Mullan H, Richards J, Lee J. Staff, associate specialist and specialty doctors' national audit on the management of gonorrhoea in the United Kingdom, 2015. Int J STD AIDS. 2017;28(14):1450-1452. doi:10.1177/0956462417710602. PMID: 28632482.

audits.title: Auditing the use and assessing the clinical utility of microscopy as a point-of-care test for Neisseria gonorrhoeae in a Sexual Health clinic.
audits.standard: Clinic protocol: urethral microscopy for male gonorrhoea contacts, urethral symptoms or epididymo-orchitis
audits.setting: Department of Sexual Health, Whittall Street Clinic, University Hospitals Birmingham

cycle1.result: Microscopy performed for 96% of contacts, 98% of those with discharge/dysuria and urethritis on examination, but only 43% of those with epididymo-orchitis.

audits.other_findings: Half of epidemiologically treated gonorrhoea contacts did not have gonorrhoea; microscopy detected 71% of heterosexual and 66% of MSM contacts with gonorrhoea.
audits.citation: Mensforth S, Thorley N, Radcliffe K. Auditing the use and assessing the clinical utility of microscopy as a point-of-care test for Neisseria gonorrhoeae in a Sexual Health clinic. Int J STD AIDS. 2018;29(2):157-163. doi:10.1177/0956462417721062. PMID: 28705094.

audits.title: 2020 BASHH national clinical audit: Management of infection with Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
audits.standard: BASHH national guidance for management of infection with Neisseria gonorrhoeae (2018), six audit standards
audits.setting: UK GUM/Integrated Sexual Health Services (level 3 STI services), BASHH national audit

cycle1.result: Standard for first-line treatment narrowly missed; the other five national audit standards were not met (no figures in abstract).

audits.other_findings: No case of possible ceftriaxone treatment failure reported to PHE.
audits.citation: Phyu K, Curtis H, Wallace H, Goodall L, Apea V, Iveson H, et al.. 2020 BASHH national clinical audit: Management of infection with Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Int J STD AIDS. 2023;34(3):203-207. doi:10.1177/09564624221139540. PMID: 36541041.
